paper.title_en: Disk-Corona Energy Balance Evolves with Flux State in the Quasar PDS 456
paper.abstract_en: We investigate the long-term X-ray spectral evolution of the highly luminous, radio-quiet quasar PDS 456 using AstroSat observations obtained in 2019 and 2021 together with archival XMM-Newton, NuSTAR and Suzaku observations spanning 2001-2024. The AstroSat observations provide valuable coverage following the bright flaring state observed in 2018, revealing that the source underwent a relatively quiescent phase in 2019 before re-brightening in 2021. During the AstroSat epochs, PDS 456 exhibits a harder-when-brighter spectral trend, whereas the long-term XMM-Newton, NuSTAR, and Suzaku observations confirm the overall softer-when-fainter behavior. This behavior is consistent with the presence of a very cool corona (~15 keV), possibly driven by a strong incident photon field for upscattering, as suggested by a prominent big blue bump. Broadband spectral modeling of simultaneous XMM-Newton and NuSTAR observations, complemented by the 2021 AstroSat flaring epoch and interpreted within the self-consistent physical framework reXcor, indicates that the disk-corona energy balance evolves with flux. In low-flux states, the spectrum is reflection-dominated, implying efficient illumination of the inner accretion disk by a compact corona. In contrast, high-flux states show an enhanced contribution from the warm Comptonizing region at larger coronal heights. The Fe Kα emission line displays a positive correlation with the 2-10 keV continuum flux at low to intermediate flux levels, while deviations at the highest flux states suggest a reduced relative reflection contribution as the warm corona becomes energetically dominant.
